chunks: ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام:
about a man who gives his zakat for dirhams in dinars, and for dinars in dirhams, according to the value—is that permissible?
He said: “There is no issue with it.”

key_terms.أَيَحِلُّ: is it permissible, asking about legal validity
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: dirhams, silver coinage used as a measure of monetary wealth
key_terms.بِالْقِيمَةِ: according to the value, meaning on the basis of equivalent worth
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: dinars, gold coinage given here as an alternative form of payment
key_terms.زَكَاتَهُ: his zakat, the obligatory alms-tax due on wealth
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no issue with it, indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay zakat in a different currency or monetary form based on equivalent value?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on paying zakat by substituting one monetary form for another according to equivalent value. It indicates that giving dinars in place of dirhams, or dirhams in place of dinars, is permissible when done on the basis of assessed value.
